title: Baseten Pricing 2026: Costs, GPUs and Token Rates
summary: Baseten pricing varies based on whether you use token-billed Model APIs or per-minute GPU deployments, making costs depend on your usage pattern.
body_markdown:
## Hidden costs and limits Baseten users hit


You will not find three things on the rate card: replica time billed while idle, latency paid on cold starts, and plan limits that cap how far you can scale. Each moves the break-even point you just saw.


### Baseten idle replica costs and autoscaling settings


If a replica is running, it is billing, whether or not it serves a request. Two settings decide how many such minutes you buy: the minimum replica count and the scale-down delay.


If the minimum is above zero, you pay for that floor around the clock, including nights and weekends.


Leave the scale-down delay long and the same thing happens more quietly, because the replica lingers after traffic drops and bills while doing nothing. Set the delay for your worst traffic spike and you've bought idle time for every ordinary day.


Read your autoscaling settings as a line item, not a tuning detail.


### Baseten cold starts versus always-on GPU replicas


Scale to zero and the idle bill goes, but the cold start comes back: the time to provision a GPU and load the weights before it can answer the first request. Larger models take longer.


The cost lands in user-facing latency, or in a minimum replica you keep warm to avoid it, which puts the idle bill back. You're choosing between paying in dollars and paying in waiting.


Plotted as monthly dollars against GPU utilisation, the always-on H100 line is flat because the replica bills regardless of traffic. The per-token API line rises with usage, and the point where they cross is break-even.


Keeping a replica warm to dodge cold starts is a decision to sit on the flat line.


Whichever setting you change, it either lifts that flat line or pushes the crossing to the right, so the break-even you calculate from the rate card is a best case.


### Baseten Model APIs rate limits and plan caps


Billing per token does not mean unlimited use: Baseten also throttles Model APIs. Request and token rate limits apply, and a workload that bursts can hit them before it comes near a budget ceiling.


You may have to move to dedicated GPUs for capacity reasons, not cost reasons, and then pay the flat line at low utilisation.


On dedicated deployments there are ceilings of their own, on concurrency and on how many replicas you can scale to. Access to particular GPU types can also depend on your plan.


Check the limits for your tier before you size a workload, because a cap you discover in production becomes an unplanned migration.


For enterprise features such as network isolation, compliance commitments and higher capacity, Baseten goes through sales, and I treat any tier I can't price without a call as an unknown. Before committing, ask in writing for:


- the minimum commitment on each plan
- the rate limits and concurrency caps that apply to you
- which GPU types your plan can reach
- any fees for the enterprise features you need


Leave an unpriced line item unasked and it can change the comparison as much as the GPU rate does.
